sources.text:
Explore the Bothnian Sea National Park and discover the nature of Finland’s most pristine marine waters, the history of former fortress islands, and the fascinating lighthouse islands.

More than 90% of the national park’s area is water. The barren islets and islands of the outer archipelago form a 160 km long narrow chain stretching from Merikarvia to Kustavi.

The Bothnian Sea National Park offers sights and experiences for the whole family, especially from spring to autumn. Many islands are ideal for boat or canoe excursions, and several can also be reached by organised boat transport.

Explore the Bothnian Sea National Park and discover the nature of Finland’s most pristine marine waters, the history of former fortress islands, and the fascinating lighthouse islands.

More than 90% of the national park’s area is water. The barren islets and islands of the outer archipelago form a 160 km long narrow chain stretching from Merikarvia to Kustavi.

The Bothnian Sea National Park offers sights and experiences for the whole family, especially from spring to autumn. Many islands are ideal for boat or canoe excursions, and several can also be reached by organised boat transport.
The most pristine marine waters in Finland
Six different archipelagos in one
Former fortress islands have a military history
Three lighthouse islands: Isokari, Kylmäpihlaja and Säppi
Some islands can also be reached even if you do not have a boat of your own
An accessible trail
Natural features of Bothnian Sea National Park
In the Bothnian Sea National Park, the earth’s upthrust significantly affects the nature. The islands are usually small in size and the waters surrounding are shallow.
Visitor's checklist
The National Park is a nature reserve
Temporary camping in the area is allowed
Overnight at the cruise port is allowed
Make campfires only in designated sites
Remember to bring a trash bag

Be prepared for areas with limited or no mobile network coverage

stops.name: Bothnian Sea National Park
stops.detail: Erkunden Sie die Bothnian Sea National Park und entdecken Sie die Natur der unberührtesten Meeresgewässer Finnlands, die Geschichte der ehemaligen Festungsinseln und die faszinierenden Leuchtturminseln. Mehr als 90% der Fläche des Nationalparks sind Wasser. Die kargen Inselchen und Inseln des äußeren Archipels bilden eine 160 km lange schmale Kette, die sich von Merikarvia bis Kustavi erstreckt. Die Bothnian Sea National Park bietet Sehenswürdigkeiten und Erlebnisse für die ganze Familie, vor allem von Frühling bis Herbst. Viele Inseln sind ideal für Boots- oder Kanuausflüge, und mehrere können auch mit einem organisierten Bootstransport erreicht werden.
